title: Dispersion — 40 MCQs
description: Pure spectrum, dispersive power of a prism material, chromatic and spherical aberration of lenses, and achromatism in lenses with its applications.

questions.q: A pure spectrum is one in which
options: the different colours are spread out without overlapping one another
the different colours overlap and mix with one another
only the red and violet colours are present
the light is not deviated at all
questions.explanation: In a pure spectrum the colours are separated by a large enough angular dispersion and are brought to focus by a convex lens, so that no two colours overlap.

questions.q: When white light passes through a glass prism, the colour that deviates the most is
questions.explanation: Violet light has the shortest wavelength and the largest refractive index in glass, so it is deviated the most; red, with the longest wavelength, deviates the least.

questions.q: The colours in the spectrum of white light, arranged in the order of increasing deviation, are
options: violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red
violet, blue, green, yellow, red, orange, indigo
red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet
red, yellow, green, blue, orange, indigo, violet
questions.explanation: The refractive index increases from red to violet, so the deviation also increases in the order red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet.

questions.q: The dispersive power ω of the material of a prism is defined by
questions.explanation: Dispersive power is the ratio of the angular dispersion to the mean deviation, which reduces to ω = (n_v − n_r)/(n_y − 1), where n_v, n_r and n_y refer to violet, red and mean (yellow) light.

questions.q: The splitting of white light into its constituent colours when it passes through a prism is called
questions.explanation: The prism refracts each colour through a slightly different angle, so the colours emerge separately and the white light is said to be dispersed.

questions.q: Dispersion of white light by a prism occurs because
options: white light consists of only two colours
the speed of all colours in glass is the same
the refractive index of the material of the prism is different for different wavelengths
the prism absorbs some colours completely
questions.explanation: Since n depends on wavelength, each colour is refracted through a different angle and the colours separate as they pass through the prism.

questions.q: In vacuum (or air), all the colours of white light travel with
options: different speeds, violet being the fastest
speeds inversely proportional to their wavelengths
questions.explanation: Vacuum is non-dispersive, so every wavelength travels with the same speed c = 3 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹; dispersion appears only in a material medium.

questions.q: Chromatic aberration of a lens is the defect in which
options: the lens absorbs the violet colour
different colours of light are brought to focus at different points
parallel rays are focused at a point on the axis
the image is formed only for red light
questions.explanation: Because the focal length of a lens depends on the refractive index, and hence on wavelength, the violet image is formed nearer the lens than the red image, giving a coloured, blurred image.

questions.q: Spherical aberration of a lens is caused by
options: the marginal rays and the paraxial rays being focused at different points on the axis
the dependence of focal length on wavelength
the lens being made of a dispersive material
total internal reflection inside the lens
questions.explanation: Rays passing through the outer (marginal) part of a spherical lens are refracted more strongly than the paraxial rays, so they meet the axis at a different point.

questions.q: An achromatic lens is a lens which is free from
questions.explanation: An achromatic combination brings two colours, usually red and violet, to the same focus, so that the image is free from coloured fringes.

questions.q: The dispersive power of the material of a prism
options: has no unit, since it is the ratio of two angles
is measured in degree per metre
questions.explanation: Dispersive power is the ratio of the angular dispersion to the mean deviation, and a ratio of two similar quantities is a pure number with no unit.

questions.q: Inside a glass prism, red light travels faster than violet light because
options: the refractive index of glass is smaller for red light than for violet light
red light has a shorter wavelength than violet light
red light is not refracted in glass
questions.explanation: Speed in the medium is v = c/n; the refractive index is smaller for red light, so red light travels faster inside the glass than violet light.

questions.q: The angular dispersion produced by a thin prism of angle A is given by
questions.explanation: The deviation of a thin prism is δ = (n − 1)A, so the angular dispersion is the difference of the deviations of violet and red light, i.e. (n_v − n_r)A.

questions.q: The chromatic aberration of a convex lens can be corrected by combining it with
options: another convex lens made of the same glass
a concave lens made of flint glass
questions.explanation: A convex lens of crown glass and a concave lens of flint glass, which has a greater dispersive power, together form an achromatic doublet in which the two colours come to a common focus.

questions.q: Spherical aberration of a lens can be reduced by
options: using a lens of larger aperture
using a stop to cut off the marginal rays
increasing the wavelength of the light used
questions.explanation: The outer rays are the ones that focus farthest from the paraxial focus, so screening off the marginal rays with a stop makes the image sharper.

A thin prism of angle 10° is made of glass for which (n_v − n_r) = 0.02. The angular dispersion produced is
questions.explanation: Angular dispersion = (n_v − n_r)A = 0.02 × 10° = 0.2°.

questions.q: A thin prism of angle 10° is made of glass of mean refractive index 1.5. The mean deviation produced is
questions.explanation: Mean deviation δ_y = (n_y − 1)A = (1.5 − 1) × 10° = 5°.

questions.q: A prism produces an angular dispersion of 0.2° and a mean deviation of 5°. The dispersive power of its material is
questions.explanation: ω = angular dispersion/mean deviation = 0.2°/5° = 0.04.

A convex lens of crown glass has focal length 20 cm and dispersive power 0.02. It is to be combined with a concave lens of flint glass of dispersive power 0.04 so that the combination is achromatic. The focal length of the flint lens must be
questions.explanation: For achromatism ω₁/f₁ + ω₂/f₂ = 0, so f₂ = −f₁ω₂/ω₁ = −20 × 0.04/0.02 = −40 cm.

questions.q: A convex lens of focal length 30 cm (ω = 0.03) is combined with a concave lens of focal length f₂ (ω = 0.05) to form an achromatic doublet. The value of f₂ is
questions.explanation: f₂ = −f₁ω₂/ω₁ = −30 × 0.05/0.03 = −50 cm; the flint lens must be concave and of greater focal length than the crown lens.

A crown glass prism of angle 6° has (n_v − n_r) = 0.02, and a flint glass prism has (n_v − n_r) = 0.03. To produce no net dispersion, the angle of the flint glass prism must be
questions.explanation: For zero net dispersion (n_v − n_r)₁A₁ = (n_v − n_r)₂A₂, so A₂ = 0.02 × 6°/0.03 = 4°.

questions.q: For two thin lenses of focal lengths f₁ and f₂ and dispersive powers ω₁ and ω₂ placed in contact, the condition for the combination to be achromatic is
questions.explanation: The chromatic aberration is removed when the dispersive powers and focal lengths satisfy ω₁/f₁ + ω₂/f₂ = 0, which requires the two lenses to be of different materials and of opposite kinds.

questions.q: A convex lens of focal length 25 cm and dispersive power 0.02 is combined with a concave lens of dispersive power 0.05 to form an achromatic doublet. The focal length of the combination is
An achromatic doublet of combined focal length 50 cm is made from a crown lens (ω = 0.02) and a flint lens (ω = 0.04). The focal lengths of the two lenses are
questions.explanation: For achromatism f₂ = −f₁ω₂/ω₁ = −2f₁. Also 1/F = 1/f₁ + 1/f₂ gives 1/50 = 1/f₁ − 1/(2f₁) = 1/(2f₁), so f₁ = +25 cm and f₂ = −50 cm.

A thin prism of angle 6° is made of glass for which n_v = 1.53, n_r = 1.51 and n_y = 1.52. The dispersive power of the glass is about
questions.explanation: ω = (n_v − n_r)/(n_y − 1) = (1.53 − 1.51)/(1.52 − 1) = 0.02/0.52 ≈ 0.038; the angle of the prism does not affect the dispersive power.

questions.q: A convex lens has a focal length of 20 cm in yellow light and the dispersive power of its material is 0.02. The difference between its focal lengths for red and violet light (f_r − f_v) is about
options: 0.4 cm, and red light is focused nearer the lens
0.2 cm, and violet light is focused nearer the lens
4 cm, and violet light is focused nearer the lens
0.4 cm, and violet light is focused nearer the lens
questions.explanation: Approximately f_r − f_v = ω f_y = 0.02 × 20 = 0.4 cm. Violet light has the larger refractive index, so its focal length is the smaller and it is focused nearer the lens.

questions.q: For a plano-convex lens used to form the image of a distant object, the spherical aberration is least when
options: the lens is turned with its axis inclined to the beam
the curved surface faces the incident parallel light
the lens is made of flint glass
the plane surface faces the incident parallel light
questions.explanation: With the curved surface towards the incident parallel beam, the refraction is divided more favourably between the two surfaces and the marginal rays are brought closer to the paraxial focus.

questions.q: An achromatic doublet of combined focal length 30 cm is made from a crown lens (ω = 0.02) and a flint lens (ω = 0.05). The focal lengths of the two lenses are
questions.explanation: For achromatism f₂ = −f₁ω₂/ω₁ = −2.5f₁, so 1/F = 1/f₁ + 1/f₂ = 1/f₁ − 1/(2.5f₁) = 0.6/f₁. With F = 30 cm this gives f₁ = 18 cm and f₂ = −45 cm.

questions.q: In an achromatic doublet a concave lens of flint glass is combined with a convex lens of crown glass because
options: flint glass absorbs the violet colour completely
the concave lens increases the converging power of the combination
flint glass has a smaller refractive index than crown glass
flint glass has a much greater dispersive power, so a weak concave lens corrects the colour defect while reducing the converging power only slightly
questions.explanation: Since ω for flint is large, only a small negative power is needed to cancel the dispersion of the crown lens, so the doublet still behaves as a converging lens of long focal length.
